signal: Turing launched Turing Frontier in April 2026 connecting AI labs with elite domain experts, and surpassed $300M ARR in a profitable year

email.body1:
Kirk, saw Turing launched Frontier connecting AI labs with elite domain experts, on the back of crossing $300M ARR profitably.

Growth that fast usually opens more North America accounts than the team can cover before the new motion ramps, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Turing off hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Kirk, quick follow-up for Turing.

With Frontier opening a new motion, North America targets usually climb faster than the team can cover. Most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to hit the number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Turing needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Kirk, last bit of proof for Turing.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Turing's reply rate likely compares to other AI software teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a North America sales motion? I will tailor it to Turing either way.
